content_html_sanitized:
Monday, January 12, 1998
See: AP Finally Makes a Story of January Report That Campus Support for Legal Cannabis

The annual UCLA nationwide survey of college freshmen  reveals that support for legalizing marijuana continues to rise among college freshmen, with 35 percent agreeing that it should be legalized. That compares with a low of 17 percent in 1989.  The fall 1997 study analyzed data from 252,082 students at 464 institutions. The first survey was taken in 1966.

College freshmen are -- of course -- just recent high school graduates, so this understates the growing recognition on campuses that marijuana prohibition is a fraud. When I was National Director of NORML and speaking frequently on campuses, I found that support for legalization cut across political lines. Remember, this is the generation that grew up on "Just Say No" and fried brains Partnership for a Drug-Free America ads. If they could not be brain washed by all of that, the prohibitionist establishment is in big trouble.
